title: India's Blind Cricket Team Boycotts Ceremony After Pakistan Awarded Washed-Out Asia Cup Final
excerpt: The Dhaka final was abandoned without a ball bowled; a technical committee's joint-winners ruling was overturned in Pakistan's favour on net run rate, and India says it will not play Pakistan until the dispute is resolved.
body:
• India's blind cricket team boycotted the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup presentation ceremony in Dhaka on Friday after Pakistan were declared champions of a final that was abandoned without a ball bowled.
  • The World Blind Cricket Council's Technical Committee had initially ruled India and Pakistan joint winners; WBCC president Syed Sultan Shah, who also chairs the Pakistan Blind Cricket Council, overturned that ruling and awarded the title to Pakistan on net run rate.
  • The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) says it will accept only the joint-winners decision and has warned India will not play Pakistan in future fixtures until the dispute is resolved.
  • Pakistan's board says the trophy was awarded in accordance with tournament rules communicated to all participating boards in November.

India's blind cricket team refused to attend the trophy presentation ceremony at the Anvir Cricket Stadium in Dhaka on Friday, November 20, after Pakistan were declared champions of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup without a single delivery being bowled in the final. Persistent rain prevented the scheduled 11:30 a.m. start, the match was abandoned, and what followed was a dispute over how a title can be decided when the final is never played.

A decision made, then overturned

According to the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), the World Blind Cricket Council's (WBCC) Technical Committee initially ruled that India and Pakistan should be declared joint winners. That decision was then overturned by WBCC president Syed Sultan Shah — who also serves as chairman of the Pakistan Blind Cricket Council — and the match referee was directed to hand the trophy solely to Pakistan on the basis of their superior net run rate in the league stage.

"This is a disgraceful decision and a blatant injustice to the Indian team. When the Technical Committee had already agreed to declare both teams joint winners, how can that decision be overturned to favour Pakistan? A title must be earned on the field."

— Mahantesh G Kivadasannavar, Chairman, CABI

CABI secretary Shailendra Yadav said India will not play Pakistan in any future fixture until the controversy is resolved. An Indian official quoted by India Today put the team's objection plainly: "Net run rate should be used for qualifiers, not to decide the winner of a final. We were suddenly informed of this decision, and we strongly oppose it."

The rule at the centre of the row

India's objections centre on the playing conditions document shared with participating teams on November 7, 2026. Indian officials argue the relevant clause was not framed correctly, was not properly highlighted in the version circulated to teams, and was never raised at the captains' meeting before the tournament. Rule 27 of the playing conditions, as reported, provides that a tied final is settled by a one-over eliminator, and that if bad weather stops the eliminator or the match is abandoned, the team with the better net run rate across the event is declared the winner.

The Pakistan Blind Cricket Council (PBCC) takes the opposite view. According to the PBCC, the organisers had communicated the rules and format of the tournament to all participating nations' boards in November, and Pakistan were adjudged champions in accordance with those rules after topping the league standings. Bangladesh Cricket Board director Abdullah Alfawad presented the awards at a closing ceremony the Indian team stayed away from.

How the two teams reached the final

Pakistan won all three of their league matches to finish top of the standings with six points and a net run rate of +4.611. In the league encounter between the two finalists on November 17, Pakistan beat India by one wicket in a close finish: chasing India's 179, they reached 180 for nine, with captain Nisar Ali scoring 64 off 51 balls. India, captained by Durga Rao Tompaki, finished second with four points and a net run rate of +4.400, and beat Bangladesh by eight wickets in their semi-final. India had entered the tournament as defending champions, having won the inaugural Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup in 2016.

What happens next

CABI has demanded that the Technical Committee's original joint-winners decision be upheld and says India will not recognise Pakistan as sole champions of the Asia Cup 2026. Its boycott warning covers future fixtures against Pakistan until the matter is resolved. The WBCC has not, in the reports so far, publicly explained the basis on which its president set aside the Technical Committee's ruling — the question on which the dispute now turns.
